clue.text: New York squad turning up to make arrest

indicators.note: in a down clue, something turning up is read from the bottom upwards, so the team name runs backwards

blocks.note: the Mets are New York's baseball team

explanation.surface: A New York police squad heading out to make an arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'squad' is not police but the New York Mets baseball team, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to halt or check it, the same sense as arresting a decline.

clue.text: Scoffed following retrospective gun control

indicators.note: retrospective means looking backwards, so the weapon's name is read in reverse

blocks.note: a Luger is a German pistol
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: Someone sneered at a backward-looking approach to gun control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' reads as mocked, but it means ate; 'following' puts it after the reversed pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: To regulate something is to govern or keep it in check, a direct synonym for the verb control.

clue.text: Black coffee ultimately providing spring

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: jet is a deep black colour
the last letter of coffee

explanation.surface: A cup of black coffee gives you a spring in your step.
explanation.walkthrough: A jeté is a ballet leap from one foot to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet a jeté is a jump, and a spring is another word for a leap or jump.

clue.text: Pushes forward version of Bros duet

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking of it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A cover of a duet by the 1980s boy band Bros gets pushed to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to thrust oneself or something forward unwelcomely, so the verb matches pushing forward.

clue.text: Fox's public display in road

indicators.note: in places the display inside the road abbreviation, which wraps around it

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a road
an expo is an exhibition

explanation.surface: A fox puts on a public show in the middle of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' looks like the animal, but in slang a fox is an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox is slang for a sexually attractive woman, which is what sexpot means.

clue.text: Quiet secretary tucking into wine that's laid down

indicators.note: something tucking into another goes inside it, so the secretary sits within the wine

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
red wine
a scribe writes things down, as a secretary does

explanation.surface: A discreet secretary helping herself to a bottle from the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid down' suggests wine stored away, but here it means set down as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed procedure is one laid down by authority, an official rule or requirement.

clue.text: Speedway tie's oddly unexciting

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered positions, the first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: taking every other letter starting with the first

explanation.surface: A drawn speedway race turns out strangely dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried, so something sedate is quiet and unexciting.

clue.text: Endlessly peruse Playboy

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to peruse is to study

explanation.surface: Reading Playboy cover to cover, over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is slang for a sexually active, womanising man, which is what a playboy is.

clue.text: This lot managed 18 around Hoylake on vacation

indicators.note: managed means handled or arranged, so the letters are rearranged
around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
on vacation means emptied out, leaving just the outer letters of the place

blocks.note: 18-across is SET
only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A golf group shepherding their players around Hoylake, a championship links, during the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoylake is a seaside town near Liverpool whose Royal Liverpool course hosts the Open golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: These is the pronoun for a group of things close at hand, the same as saying this lot.

clue.text: Management of Real Betis is most unfocused

indicators.note: management suggests organising or arranging, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the football club's name

explanation.surface: The board running the Spanish football club Real Betis has lost all direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are blurred and unfocused, so the superlative describes the most unfocused.

clue.text: A peripheral role in return game

indicators.note: in return means coming back the other way, so the word for a role is read backwards

blocks.note: a computer mouse is a peripheral device
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: An actor in a small supporting role in a return match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peripheral' reads as an adjective (minor), but it is a noun: a device plugged into a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse Trap is a long-running children's board game in which players build a contraption to catch mice.

clue.text: Scrap pile somewhere in London

blocks.note: first meaning: a broken fragment, as of pottery or glass
second meaning: the tall glass skyscraper by London Bridge

explanation.surface: A scrapheap somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pile' is a large building; the Shard is London's tallest skyscraper, near London Bridge station.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp broken piece, a scrap, and the Shard is the name of the London tower.

clue.text: Topless experience in bar is heavily criticised

indicators.note: topless means with the top taken off, so the first letter goes
in places the shortened word inside the one for a bar

blocks.note: a rod is a bar
to taste something is to experience it

explanation.surface: Someone's visit to a topless bar earns them a public dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless bar' looks like a single phrase, but 'Topless' applies to the experience and the bar is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise or mock them severely, so roasted means heavily criticised.

clue.text: Son in row over another exam

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word for a row runs backwards
in places the son inside the turned-round row

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son arguing with his parents about having to take yet another exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a second sitting of an exam that was failed, so it is another exam.

clue.text: Racket affected service returns — netting 6 in 18

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of the noise are put into a new order
returns means comes back the other way, so the service call is read backwards
netting means catching inside, so the number sits within the other letters

blocks.note: a let is a tennis serve that clips the net and is replayed
a racket is a loud noise
VI is 6 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A tennis match where the racket and returns are spoiled, with the net catching the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Racket, service, returns and netting all suggest tennis. The definition is the cross-reference 18, which is SET, as in a TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: A television is commonly called a set, the answer to 18-across.

clue.text: Setter's construction is most succinct

indicators.note: a construction is something built up, so the letters are assembled in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of the word, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The compiler boasts that their crossword is the most concise.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and to the point, so the superlative is the most succinct.

clue.text: Short movie sent up Animal House

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien
a sty is a house for pigs

explanation.surface: A trimmed version of the comedy Animal House parodied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an instruction to cut the movie, but it is the definition: brusque.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short with someone means being curt and irritable, which is what testy means.

clue.text: Nerve of pilot changing direction

indicators.note: a direction change from right to left swaps the letter for right for the letter for left

blocks.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it

explanation.surface: It takes nerve for a pilot to change course.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) becomes L (left). Both words are verbs here: to steel oneself is to nerve oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To nerve yourself and to steel yourself both mean to summon courage for something.

clue.text: Teachers' paperback collection

indicators.note: back means the teachers' paper is read backwards

blocks.note: the TES (Times Educational Supplement) is the British teachers' weekly paper, here read back to front

explanation.surface: A teachers' collection of paperback books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paperback' splits into paper and back.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a group of things belonging together, a collection.

clue.text: Most posh wine shops getting into alcohol-free

indicators.note: getting into means going inside, so the shops sit within the abstainer's abbreviation

blocks.note: TT means teetotal
offies is British slang for off-licences, shops selling alcohol

explanation.surface: Upmarket wine merchants are starting to stock alcohol-free drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A toff is a posh person, and toffy describes someone upper-class, so toffiest is most posh.

clue.text: Bet24 sponsors

blocks.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
24-down is SECOND, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: An online betting firm named Bet24 sponsoring a team.
explanation.walkthrough: Bet24 looks like a bookmaker's name; it splits into bet and the cross-reference 24.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who backs a venture funds or supports it, as a sponsor does.

clue.text: Run along banks of canal like Van Gogh?

indicators.note: the banks of a waterway are its edges, so only the outer letters are used

blocks.note: the first and last letters
Van Gogh famously cut off part of his ear

explanation.surface: Running along a canal bank like the painter Van Gogh in Arles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run along' reads as jogging beside the canal, but it is the dismissive order to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Run along and clear off are both brusque orders telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Dozens of mischievous creatures chasing short couple

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: a couple is two
elves are mischievous little folk

explanation.surface: Lots of naughty sprites pursuing a little couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' puts the creatures behind the shortened couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is a group of twelve, so dozens are twelves.

clue.text: Golfer upset over new tee for tournaments

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the golfer's name reads upwards
over means lying across and covering, so the golfer's name wraps the other letters

blocks.note: Seve Ballesteros, the Spanish golfer
n is the abbreviation for new
tee is the name of the letter T

explanation.surface: A golfer annoyed at a new tee being installed for competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting tournaments are often called events, as in a golf or athletics event.

clue.text: Instant mousse conditioner bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the answer is contained in the phrase

blocks.note: inside the two words, across the gap

explanation.surface: Hair mousse with built-in conditioner sold in bottles, instant results.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant and a second are both very short moments of time.

clue.text: Restless Cooler King escapes totally exhausted

indicators.note: escapes means gets out, so the letter for king leaves the word
exhausted means emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: a fridge is a cooler
R (rex) is king, and here it is removed
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Steve McQueen's Cooler King gets restless after escaping, totally worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cooler King is McQueen's character in the film The Great Escape, but cooler here is a fridge and the king is R.
explanation.definitionFit: A fidgety person keeps moving and cannot stay still, which is to be restless.

clue.text: Game of skill caught old Nazi

blocks.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Rudolf Hess, Hitler's deputy

explanation.surface: A tactical game in which an old Nazi was captured.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game decided purely by skill, with no element of chance.

clue.text: Dope left in bed

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the word for the bed

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
l is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An idiot left lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, and a clot is British slang for the same.

clue.text: Having no issue with Kid Rock initially in charge

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
in puts the kept letter inside the word for a charge

blocks.note: a kid is a child
a fee is a charge
the first letter

explanation.surface: The rapper Kid Rock has no problem being first in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is legal language for offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a person's issue are their children, so having no issue means having no children.

clue.text: Blue swallow heading south

blocks.note: first meaning: sad or low
second meaning: to gulp a drink in one
third meaning: going in a downward direction

explanation.surface: A sad-looking swallow flying south for the winter.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two; the swallow is not a bird but the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sad, to drink in one gulp, and moving lower, and is also the heading of this clue list.

clue.text: Sylvester Stallone's hiding at first

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so the answer lies inside the actor's name

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first name and the start of the surname

explanation.surface: Sylvester Stallone was in hiding in his early days.
explanation.definitionFit: Erst is an archaic word for formerly or at first, used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Expenditure of friendly society

blocks.note: an outgoing person is sociable and friendly
s is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: The spending of a friendly society, a British mutual savings club.
explanation.walkthrough: A friendly society is a British mutual insurance association, which makes the clue read as a single phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are money paid out, which is expenditure.

clue.text: Threads to stitch contrary wrapping paper

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the verb for stitching is read backwards
wrapping means enclosing, so the reversed verb surrounds the newspaper

blocks.note: to stitch is to sew
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Using thread to sew wrapping paper, which refuses to cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrapping paper' reads as gift wrap, but wrapping is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wefts are the crosswise threads woven through the warp on a loom.
